sql_schemas: table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; approved_by -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: frequent lookups of all leave requests for a given employee; status: filtering and counting requests by status (PENDING, APPROVED, REJECTED); leave_type: filtering requests by type (annual, sick, emergency); start_date, end_date: range queries for date-overlap validation and reporting periods; employee_id, status: combined filtering for manager dashboards showing pending approvals per team

table employees | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: email: unique lookup for authentication and employee search; employee_number: unique lookup by employee number; manager_id: hierarchical queries — find direct reports for a manager; employment_status: filtering active/inactive/terminated employees; department: grouping and filtering by department

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, policy_id, total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, fiscal_year, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; policy_id -> leave_policies.id | indexes: employee_id: look up all balances for a given employee; employee_id, fiscal_year: determine current-year balance for an employee; policy_id: look up all balances tied to a specific policy; employee_id, policy_id, fiscal_year: unique constraint support — one balance row per employee/policy/year

table leave_policies | fields: id, policy_name, leave_type, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: leave_type: look up active policy for a given leave type; is_active: filtering only active policies; leave_type, is_active: combined filter for the default/active policy per type

table audit_logs | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, old_values, new_values, performed_by, performed_at, ip_address, user_agent, created_at | pk: id | indexes: entity_type, entity_id: look up all audit records for a specific entity; performed_by: look up all actions by a specific user; performed_at: time-range queries for audit reports; action: filtering by action type (CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, APPROVE, REJECT)

data_notes: Five conceptual tables defined: leave_requests, employees, leave_balances, leave_policies, audit_logs. Each table spec includes field names, primary key, foreign-key relationships, and index rationale driven by access patterns (employee lookups, status filtering, date-range overlap checks, fiscal-year balance queries, audit trails). Five repository interfaces with concrete PostgreSQL implementations via pg Pool: ILeaveRequestRepository/PgLeaveRequestRepository, ILeaveBalanceRepository/PgLeaveBalanceRepository, ILeavePolicyRepository/PgLeavePolicyRepository, IEmployeeRepository/PgEmployeeRepository, IAuditLogRepository/PgAuditLogRepository. All repositories use the shared db connection at src/shared/db/connection.ts. Audit logging (GP-002) is covered by IAuditLogRepository. The leave_requests table supports the batch-fix validation feature via findOverlapping for date-conflict detection and updateStatus for batch approval/rejection. leave_balances supports upsert for atomic balance adjustments during leave approval/rejection.
